\n- owns: `<sub>/state/<name>/<id>`;

\n- writes: `<sub>/<manifest:unit.rows>/<id>` (guard), `<sub>/state/<name>/<id>` (guard), `objects/<sub>/commands/<rid>` (mark), `<sub>/requests/<rid>` (create), `<events root>/<sub>/<unit>/e<epoch>/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>.events.jsonl` (append), `<events root>/<sub>.alarms/<unit>/e<epoch>/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>.events.jsonl` (append), `<events root>/audit/<role>/e1/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>.events.jsonl` (append), `<events root>/audit.alarms/<role>/e1/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>.events.jsonl` (append), `objects/<sub>/<manifest:objects.rows>/*` (cas), `<events or objects root>/<path>/%h<sha256>.name` (create);
\n- reads: `<sub>/requests/<rid>`, `platform/manifest/<sub>`, `<sub>/requests/free-<server>-<volume>`.
\nThe row-object written by the training append handler follows [P/05](../../05-resource/spec/05-resource.norms.md) N1.1 `row_object`.
\n**Event suppression: `kinds`.** The platform does not judge the severity of `events.kinds.<kind>` and does not write that severity into the event line.
\n**Event suppression: `by`.** without by — all fields of the line except t/id/repeats/since/until
\n**Event suppression: `by`.** Naming any of `t`, `id`, `repeats`, `since`, `until` in `by`, or giving an empty `by`, is a load refusal.
\n**Event suppression: `rule`.** repeats are counted
\n**Event suppression: `rule`.** In the suppression summary, `since` is `t` of the first event line of that window.
\n**Event suppression: `rule`.** In the suppression summary, `until` is `t` of the last swallowed repeat.
\n**Event suppression: `rule`.** In the suppression summary, `t` is the moment when the summary is written.
\n**Event suppression: `rule`.** a window without repeats gives no line
\n**Event suppression: `rule`.** the summary of the previous window is written before the first line of the new one
\n**Event suppression: `stop`.** a window without repeats gives no line
\nThe name unit in by is the unit from the writer's arguments/the bucket path, not a user field\nof the line of the same name.
\nThe other names of by are the top fields of the written line;\nan unknown/absent field gives a separate value «absent», distinct from null.
\nThe comparison is structural JSON: an object without regard to the order of keys, an array with regard to the order,\na bool is not a number.
\nThe absence of a selected field in a particular event is not a manifest error. t/id and the\nsummary fields do not take part; when by is absent, the other fields, including occurred/of, take part.
\nWhen, about what and with which fields to order is the logic\nof subsystem C (its lesson); here — what the library does with each order (N3 «order»).
\n**Customer order: `order`.** the fields F of the row of A — without the id source field of A, without *_secret and blob
\n**Customer order `key`.** In the notation `values_by_type` of the row check contract, `int` is decimal; the resulting field notation is then byte-encoded by P/03.6-R224.
\n**Customer order `key`.** In the notation `values_by_type` of the row check contract, `float` follows its choice rule; the resulting field notation is then byte-encoded by P/03.6-R224.
\n**Customer order `key`.** In the notation `values_by_type` of the row check contract, `bool` is `true | false`; the resulting field notation is then byte-encoded by P/03.6-R224.

\nFor every field type in P/03.6-R089, P/03.6-R090, P/03.6-R091 and P/03.6-R092, encode every UTF-8 byte of the field notation outside `A–Z a–z 0–9 _ . ~` as `%XX`, with hex digits in upper case (`-` → `%2D`, `%` → `%25`). This byte encoding precedes the joining of substitutions in P/03.6-R093.
\n**Customer order `key`.** Join the byte-encoded substitutions of `worker.creates[].key` from P/03.6-R224 with the literal «-» between them.
\n**Customer order `key`.** Different values of the fields give different ids, so the id determines these values: a returned name is the same subject.
\n**Customer order: `fields`.** the id source field — with the ready id
\n**Customer order: `fields`.** *_secret are never written — they stay empty, the secret is set by the operator through the door
\n**Customer order: `fields`.** blob are empty (P/06.1 N1.5)
\n**Customer order: `until`.** If the manifest of A declares `placement.ends`, extend its deadline field `placement.ends.field` by max(the previous, the new).
\n**Customer order: `until`.** If the manifest of A declares `placement.ends` and the previous deadline is `never` (without a deadline), leave that value untouched.
\n**Customer order: `deletes`.** When deleting by `worker.deletes` a row without `made`, the addressee worker uses CAS of its read version, as before.
\n**Customer order `guard`.** After the store is restored, the guard version can coincide — the lease checks the floor.
\n**Customer order: `writers`.** a row of its own made may be extended by any unit of C
\n**Customer order: `writers`.** a row without its own made is taken: C does not write it
\n**Customer order: `check`.** The reads of the common row check derive from the declaration (the rights — P/02.5 N1.4).
\nThe declaration is `unit.state: {<name>: <schema>}` (P/02.1 N1.2a); `cursor` is the cursor\nof the unit.
\nThe start snapshot is immutable: born/revision/epoch and the guard version come from the accepted start, never a newer read.
\nReading the state CAS version and performing IO are the state-write steps P/03.6-R193 and P/03.6-R194; construction of key/items/guard is P/03.6-R192, and value validation is P/03.6-R029.
\n**Unit state: `row`.** the family is state.schema.json
\n**Unit state: `writer`.** born and revision — of the start, not of the re-read unit row: a cut-off holder, also by a late replay, will not overwrite the state of the new epoch
\n**Unit state: `cursor`.** unit.state.cursor acts by born (revision is not compared: an edit of the row does not reset the cursor)
\n**Unit state: `cursor`.** monotonic — the meaning of the value is set by the subsystem
\n**Unit state: `cursor`.** survives a move
\n**Unit state: `STATE_EVERY`.** runtime-constants.tsv state write cadence

\nThe doors of requests, events and acknowledgements are the console and\nthe resource (the doors of the resource — P/05 N2; the doors of the console — [P/06.4](../../06-console/spec/06.4-console.norms.md) N2).
\nOne holder's look processes `≤ COMMANDS_PER_LOOK` commands.
\nA limit: `at` is the filer's clock, two consoles with a clock skew do not keep the order, and for `at` of one second the order is given by `rid`; rows of different groups are not ordered.
\n**Step 6.** The order of the checks: a mark with an outcome, `most_valid`, a foreign `begun`, then the deadline.

\n**Step 8.** The holder checks before the call the deadline (`valid_until` in the past → `expired`; beyond `most_valid` → `refused`), the stamp `group` and its own epoch\nof the unit — it takes only the rows of the units that it leads under its own lease.

\n**Step 10.3.** This is the protocol of one holder process epoch; elapsed timeout plus grace does not establish completion of an older holder call or cross-holder exclusion (P/03.6-R163, P/03.6-R165 and P/03.6-R166).
\nThe possible overlap of calls from successive holders is explicit; no cross-holder exclusion is promised.
\nThe guarantee of repeats is limited by the time the mark is kept: after its lawful cleanup\nthe client does not reuse rid/Idempotency-Key and does not pass off a new filing as a confirmed repeat.
\nA repeat after the removal is admitted and is again checked against the data; the guarantee\n«one call through the mark» does not apply to it.
\nIts columns `word`, `cause`, `outcome`, `diagnostic`, `caller` are the normative cells of a refusal, the rows in file order; `-` is an absent cell.
\nMachine columns identify the surface and any fixed code.
\nA `peer` surface refers to the imported door contract; it creates no HTTP API of the worker.
\n**Training customer: `tally_order`.** For a `testsub` counter with `start ≥ 1000`, the ordered `testsub2/tallies` row id is `testsub-<of>`.
\n**Training customer: `tally_order`.** A repeated start of a `testsub` counter with `start ≥ 1000` is a new event and extends `until` of its ordered `testsub2/tallies` row.
\n**Training customer: `tally_order`.** counters with start < 1000 do not order
\n**Training append handler: `ranges`.** With no covered segments, `ranges` is the empty string "".

The rows `notes`, `rolls` are under the guard
of the slot; the object `counts` — without CAS (objects have no guards, as with the heartbeat), it is written only by the holder of a confirmed slot,
